text: I'm not going to sugarcoat it; I've been using this software for roughly 5 months and I still Google what functions are located where, simply because menu items are frequently changed between updates. The “free” “One App” version is essentially designed to get your foot in the door and immediately requires you to upgrade to the next level of service (which costs).

horrible experience. Salesman oversold the capabilities of the self help tools and how it was a useful software for micro companies. Unless you have 10 or more employees and can dedicate one person to spend tens and tens of hours on implementation, stay away. Odoo seems to be set up to attract a customer at a low price, and then force them to spend thousands of dollars on their hourly support as the self help is useless. You will spend multiples more than the initial payment to Odoo. We asked for a refund after only a few weeks due to the salesman's over sell and poor self help tools, but they refused. I tried to reach out to corporate management but they will not respond to communications. They just want the money coming in. The Odoo concept seems good, they just cannot produce what they sell.

Terrible experience with this company. Their software is over complicated and implementation process was terrible. They promised it would be an easy to use software while selling however the final product has a terrible user interface. Make sure you avoid the sales executive, Samwise Geida, who will say anything for you to close the deal. Complete crooks, I would not recommend to anyone.
Odoo can be complex to set up and customize, and some features require technical knowledge. The learning curve can be steep, and certain integrations may need additional configuration.
Documentation is no better than useless. It took me three hours of trial-and-error to set up multiple currencies using shipping tax rates.

We faced a technical issue during the integration of one of the modules. The data wasn't flowing in. We tried to reach customer support, but the response was unexpectedly very slow. As new modules are on-boarded, more assistance would be required. Odoo needs to work on this aspect to make it better.

We’re charged per user each month and for certain Apps. Every time I think “that sounds great,” I find out we need another App. I know of people who made a field in Studio only to have to reverse-engineer it 6 months later. Searching large databases is also slow. They load the entire page first, before allowing me to filter anything, so I just sit there waiting for the spinner rather than performing my duties. Pet Peeve: Each application looks somewhat different. The buttons move around, and even after using the software for 2 years, I still occasionally press the wrong corner.

My overall experience is mixed. The software itself is very good and has strong potential, but the consulting experience was disappointing. I expected the consultant to bring expertise, understand our business processes, and help us translate our needs into a practical Odoo setup. Instead, I often spent more time and energy trying to obtain clear answers than I saved by using the consulting service. After 25 hours, I did not feel that we had reached a sufficiently concrete or useful configuration for our company. My main disappointment was the consulting service. I purchased a 25-hour consulting package for about €1,450 after a 15% discount. Unfortunately, I felt that a significant part of those hours was not used for real consulting. In several cases, even for relatively standard Odoo questions, the assigned consultant had to ask internal colleagues for help, and all of that time was deducted from my package.

The main issue for me was the learning curve. Odoo has so many modules, menus and configuration options that the first experience can feel more complicated than expected. Some simple tasks took me longer because I had to understand how Odoo structures the workflow first.
I can be a daunting ecosystem for new developers. The level of complexity for seamingly simple operations can be overwhelming.

It's as bad as Albonomics in Australia, only worse. Fancy being charged a premium, to populate yoru subscription to use what you paid for Our fee went from $567/yr to over $5000 per year So then we had to delete all the work we paid for Was an experience that cost thousands in dollars and 6 months in time, for no outcome. The onlytime they return contact is to hit you with the mother of all invoices. Just avoid. It is not worth it

their invoicing is very unclear: they suddenly more than doubled our monthly costs because a tiny part of our operation was in a more expensive country. Very unexpected and completely inflexible, we feel very misled in this case. This only surfaced months into our collaboration, when it's hard to pull back out.

The main drawback is that Odoo can take some time to configure and learn, especially when using multiple modules or advanced features. Some workflows are not immediately intuitive, and customization can require technical knowledge. There can also be occasional performance issues or bugs, particularly with larger databases or more complex configurations. Customer support and pricing flexibility could also be improved.

Odoo essentially blocks you from changing the core coding so if your company has a unique or "weird" way of completing processes then you will need to completely change how your company completes those processes. The on-boarding experience was horrible. On Black Friday, when we were doing our first major use of the system during peak season, the cloud synchronization between the e-commerce frontend and the warehouse logistics literally ran a continuous spinning circle on its loading wheel for 10 minutes straight, and made us appear like complete idiots to the people who were calling in.

When viewing things at the top level, I dislike seeing where an invoice belongs to within an entity since you cannot tell while running a report. Also, the tools used for creating your own custom reports are completely frustrating.

What I liked least about Odoo is that some features can feel a bit rough or not fully polished, and you sometimes need technical skills to customize things properly. Also, performance can slow down with many modules, and support isn't always super responsive.
I have had mixed responses to customer support. I asked some technical questions on transaction management a couple of times and the responses I received were so vague that they were not helpful.
Major version updates regularly bring frustrating technical bugs to customized modules. Furthermore, subscription costs accelerate quickly as you stack applications and users.

Don't waste your time with Odoo... most people who recommend it are being paid a referral fee... the support is extremely slow and almost non-existent in my experience and the services are slow and difficult to learn... I have wasted hundreds on dollars on Odoo and hope you don't make the same mistake. The software is difficult to work out and use, documentation is poor... it is expensive once you start adding things on and support is terrible.
Customer support feels bit slow with lower price subscriptions. With Higher plans subscription the customer service is feaster somehow.

Solid foundation is a joke. OpenERP is probably one of the shittiest pieces of code every written in Python. Take a look at their ORM code. And, of course they still use floating points for accounting.
Snarky comments aside, where odoo falls down is that it tries to be everything and do everything and unsurprisingly falls short if you compare it to a single purpose application.

Please don't get me started on Odoo. We've tried to use Odoo as the base system for an ERP for a customer from us. Then one of our bosses had the idea to update to Odoo, because it was the "current version". I've hardly seen such a half ass job of documenting the new version. The last time I was working on it the only "documentation" was a 3 page presentation from the Odoo days. Half of the plugins we used with OpenERP didn't work any more, and some functionality was in the GUI (updating plugins) but didn't work (in a stable and released version). When searching for answers Stackoverflow didn't really work and the whole vibe in the forums was along the line "I've finally got it working - it was not that hard after I found out how to do it" or "you just have to pay company x a certain amount they will gladly do that for you".

Odoo, for example, is "open source" until you need "enterprise" things. Well, it turns out you can point a robot at it and just add those things on your own now. Bonus for releasing your fork under the same license as the community edition... Strange times.

I like that Odoo is easy to navigate, but each of their apps feels like a cookie cutter CRUD implementation rather than something designed by people who understand the problems really well. For example, we started with our contacts app and it's really hard to get right. It has to be fast, getting to any contact should take 2 clicks maximum. Search results are tailored to your search. The entire contacts list is virtualized at the DOM and data layer - you can scroll through 10s of thousands of contacts without having to mash prev/next page. We put a ton of care into each field - each field is smart.

Another detail to improve from my point of view would be when generating the electronic guides, although we have a good order, it sometimes happens that the same system separates certain products and makes jumps in the correlatives of the guide numbers, and this could generate inconveniences if we have an audit. And another point to improve is that sometimes when the release guide for a product is being issued, this product is not discounted from the actual inventory stock, I don't know if it is an internal error, but it has been happening and it happened very frequently a couple of years ago.

I would like to see easier to configure email templates that do not require a coding background to edit / manipulate. The Email to CRM pipeline often has issues pulling from our shared gmail inbox. We struggle alot with duplicate customer profiles and find that it is hard to keep a company profile organized when there are multiple private emails associated with that company.
Integrating WhatsApp API should be more easy

It would be great if one could load Marketplace Modules on Odoo.online. Documentation is lacking for customers that want to do self-serivce on Odoo.online. Not having product dimensions as standard feature is a major downfall.
POS is missing a lot of functionality. Can be glitchy. Seems to do MOST of everything. But has gaps.

Customer service is nonexistent. You will need a 3rd party to assist you. The system has an open app for integrating with other programs. These are developed by third parties and can be hit or miss in functionality. The system offers great flexibility; however, it is too much and requires coding. For example, changing a Sales order PDF requires coding to modify the document. Initial implementation is clunky and seems to require a 3rd party just for setup. Implementation was a terrible experience for us. Because it required a third party, we ended up way over budget and schedule.

What a horrible company! The first interaction I had with the human at this company was to tell me that the purchase we made was too little and that they were going to charge us double or erase everything we've done! When they spoke to me, they claimed that their website charged the wrong amount because our company operates in different countries and therefore they would be doubling the price. However, when we made the purchase it was specified in writing exactly how much we would have to pay. I guess they don't honour their own terms of service. terrible customer service. In my experience, they don't even honour their own terms of service.
